source.title: Signal propagation in continuous approximations of binary neural networks
source.authors: G. Stamatescu; Federica Gerace; Carlo Lucibello; I. Fuss; L. White

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The title in the supplied metadata differs from the paper title shown in the text; the text is a paper published at ICLR 2020.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether initialization affects signal propagation and training performance in binary-network surrogates, using a different model setting and measure from V4’s conventional deep networks.
record.gate_note: The study’s MNIST training-performance sweeps bear on V4. CIFAR-10/100 training error, teacher-student local minima, shortcut comparisons, above-stability-limit learning rates, and batch-normalization speed claims are not tested. Theoretical critical-initialization results and the random-network simulations are not separate task-training results.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4's initialization–trainability relationship in a new setting: continuous surrogates of binary networks. Its MNIST experiments vary initialization and depth and report training performance consistent with predicted signal-propagation depth scales.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but omits a central distinction: the deterministic surrogate for binary weights and neurons admits critical initialization, whereas the corresponding LRT surrogate does not. LRT with binary weights and continuous tanh neurons does admit it. The authors recommend weight means near ±1 and bias variance near zero, and report qualitative training evidence plus a depth-dependent performance gap between surrogates and binary counterparts.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains binary-network surrogates while varying the variance of binary-weight means and depth; its experiments use MNIST rather than the benchmark and initialization procedures described in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Training performance varies with binary-weight-mean variance and depth; the text says deeper networks require smaller learning rates and more training time, while the experiment holds epochs fixed.

fits_no_version.finding: Binary counterparts perform worse than the continuous surrogate, particularly at greater depth; increasing Monte Carlo samples from five to 100 brings performance closer to the surrogate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training a continuous surrogate does not ensure equivalent classification performance in its binary counterpart; evaluation sampling affects the gap.

record.problems: The training experiments use MNIST and only 10 epochs (or 5 for the surrogate-versus-binary comparison). The authors characterize the depth comparison as qualitative because training time and suitable learning rates vary with depth. Performance values are presented in figures without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible result rows left out. The mean-field equations and random-network signal-propagation simulations are theoretical or initialization diagnostics, not separate training-performance results.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and model-size or training-recipe qualifications.
Spurious local minima and the benefit of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth degradation with and without identity shortcuts, very deep plain tanh training, and normalization-free residual training.

Conventional activation-matched initialization comparisons, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer convolutional training. Fixed 10-epoch experiments do not establish eventual convergence or arbitrary-depth trainability.
Recovery above the initial stability threshold, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. Equal training budgets across depths and the need for smaller learning rates in deeper networks limit what the experiments establish, but do not themselves show V4 failing. The theoretical and initialization-diagnostic results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100, corrupted or random labels, model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and extra student neurons.
Plain versus residual networks, shortcut effects, very deep plain tanh training, and normalization-free residual training.

The experiments vary binary-weight-mean initialization and network depth in surrogate models on MNIST, but do not test activation-matched conventional initializations, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates above the stability threshold, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch-normalization speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.
